record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let CTCS(n) be the continuous-time critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, obtained by recursively splitting a clade of m leaves into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probabilities proportional to 1/(i(m-i)), and let D_n^(1) and D_n^(2) be the time-heights of two leaves whose positions in the interval/cycle representation are r_n apart. If log r_n / log n -> alpha in [0,1], prove that the correlation coefficient rho(n,r_n) between these two leaf heights converges to 1-alpha.

evidence.quote: Open problems1 are noted throughout, and enumerated separately as Open Problems 1 - 20.
Open Problem 1 Prove that, for log rn/log n → α ∈ [0, 1], we have ρ(n, rn) → 1 − α. (40)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the continuous-time critical beta-splitting random tree on $n$ leaves, denoted $\mathrm{CTCS}(n)$, as follows. Starting from a single clade containing all $n$ leaves, each clade of size $m\ge 2$ persists for an exponential holding time of rate $h_{m-1} = \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j$, after which it splits into two subclades of sizes $i$ and $m-i$ ($1\le i\le m-1$) with probability
\[
q(m,i) \;=\; \frac{1}{h_{m-1}}\cdot\frac{1}{i(m-i)}\cdot\frac{m}{2}\cdot\mathbf{1}\{1\le i\le m-1\}\cdot\tfrac{1}{?}\,,
\]
i.e. proportional to $1/(i(m-i))$ (with the appropriate symmetric normalization so that probabilities sum to one); subclades evolve independently in the same manner, and clades of size $1$ are leaves and do not split further. The time-height of a leaf is the sum of the holding times of the clades containing it (equivalently, the time at which that leaf is created).

Use the natural ``interval'' (or cyclic) representation in which the $n$ leaves are placed in a fixed linear order $1,2,\dots,n$ induced by the recursive splitting. For $1\le r\le n-1$, let $D_n^{(1)}$ and $D_n^{(2)}$ denote the time-heights of two leaves whose positions in this order are at distance $r_n$ apart, and let
\[
\rho(n,r_n) \;=\; \mathrm{Corr}\bigl(D_n^{(1)},\,D_n^{(2)}\bigr).
\]

Prove that whenever $r_n$ is a sequence of integers with $1\le r_n\le n-1$ and
\[
\frac{\log r_n}{\log n} \longrightarrow \alpha \in [0,1] \qquad (n\to\infty),
\]
one has
\[
\rho(n,r_n)\;\longrightarrow\;1-\alpha.
\]
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an explicit open problem in the overview paper on the critical beta-splitting random tree and subsequent works (Aldous–Pittel on heights, Aldous–Janson on Mellin analysis, and a contraction-based approach) treat related limit theorems for single-leaf heights but do not appear to resolve this two-leaf correlation conjecture. No published proof of the limit $\rho(n,r_n)\to 1-\alpha$ was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 1: Prove that, for log r_n/log n → α ∈ [0,1], we have ρ(n,r_n) → 1 − α.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as Open Problem 1 in the overview/open-problems paper.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree IV: Mellin analysis of Leaf Height
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp asymptotic distributions for the height of a uniform random leaf via Mellin analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses single-leaf height asymptotics, not the two-leaf correlation limit.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Alternative proofs of the CLT for random leaf height using the contraction method.
status_evidence.claim: Provides CLTs for one-leaf heights but does not establish the conjectured correlation limit.
